country.comment: Analyses Brazilian municipalities across all five macro-regions that directly provide water and wastewater services without delegating to state-owned or private utilities.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 2, Section 1; PDF p. 4, Section 3.1

effect_estimate.comment: Exact coefficients and municipality-clustered robust standard errors reported from Tables 3–6 (N = 1,720 municipality-years across 344 municipalities, 2015–2019). Authors note estimates represent conditional associations rather than definitive causal effects.
effect_estimate.value: In baseline two-way fixed-effects models (N = 1,720 observations across 344 municipalities, 2015–2019), binary participation in intermunicipal cooperation (IMC) is not significantly associated with water coverage (WC: β = −0.094, SE = 0.920, p ≥ 0.10), wastewater coverage (WWC: β = −2.311, SE = 2.189, p ≥ 0.10), or service quality/inverse water loss index (QUA: β = 4.929, SE = 3.219, p ≥ 0.10), and has a negative association with the revenue-to-expense financial ratio (FIN: β = −7.253, SE = 3.721, p < 0.10). By contrast, each additional year of IMC duration (IMCd) in fixed-effects models is positively associated with water coverage (WC: β = 0.570 percentage points/year, SE = 0.283, p < 0.05) and wastewater coverage (WWC: β = 0.880 percentage points/year, SE = 0.485, p < 0.10), not significantly associated with FIN (β = 1.685, SE = 1.081, p ≥ 0.10; positive in random-effects: β = 0.995, SE = 0.550, p < 0.10), and negatively associated with service quality (QUA: β = −0.940 index points/year, SE = 0.528, p < 0.10, reflecting higher water losses over time; random-effects IMC β = 4.560, SE = 2.281, p < 0.05 and IMCd β = −0.577, SE = 0.268, p < 0.05).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Appraised with ROBINS-I, the study has at least Serious risk of bias due to uncontrolled time-varying municipal confounders (lnPOP is the sole time-varying covariate; only 17 of 344 municipalities switched IMC status over 5 years; no pre-trend verification; and authors explicitly state estimates reflect conditional relationships rather than definitive causal effects), capping certainty below 3. Because the study relies solely on secondary municipal datasets (MUNIC and SNIS) without directly observing internal consortium administrative or organizational learning mechanisms, certainty is 1 (documented statistical association).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; PDF pp. 5–6, Section 3.2 & Section 4; PDF p. 8, Section 6

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines horizontal intermunicipal cooperation (IMC) via public consortia and cooperation duration (IMCd) among local municipal providers to overcome fragmented municipal scale constraints and coordinate WWS provision. None of the four household-facing top-level family codes (ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, ENFORCEMENT) are directly measured, as the studied institutional mechanism operates solely at the inter-municipal governance/coordination level (political_coordination, institutional_fragmentation).
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 1–4, Sections 1–3.1 & Table 1; PDF pp. 7–8, Sections 5–6

outcome_flags.comment: Directly measures municipal water coverage (% served population, WC), wastewater coverage (% served population, WWC), and service quality (inverse distribution water-loss index, QUA). Financial outcome (FIN) measures utility operational revenue-to-expense cost recovery rather than household tariff affordability.

publication_year.comment: Explicitly printed in journal citation header, dates block, and copyright line on every page.

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Evaluates municipal participation in and duration of a specific institutional governance arrangement (intermunicipal cooperation via public consortia) against comparator municipalities without IMC using two-way panel fixed-effects (municipality and year fixed effects) plus random-effects and Mundlak correlated random-effects specifications, matching ROBINS-I for policy panel fixed-effects designs with a comparator.

sample_size.comment: Balanced 5-year panel (2015–2019) from IBGE MUNIC and SNIS covering 344 municipalities (6.2% of all 5,570 Brazilian municipalities and 23.4% of municipalities directly providing WWS), yielding 1,720 municipality-year observations.
sample_size.value: 344 municipalities (local water and wastewater service providers); 1,720 municipality-year observations (balanced 5-year panel, 2015–2019; 308 observations across 71 municipalities participating in IMC, including 17 joining during the period, and 1,412 observations without IMC)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 4, Section 3.1 & Table 2; PDF p. 5, Section 3.2

study_design.comment: Quantitative longitudinal panel econometric analysis of secondary municipal administrative datasets (MUNIC and SNIS, 2015–2019) comparing municipalities participating and not participating in intermunicipal cooperation arrangements and testing duration of cooperation.
study_design.value: Balanced panel-data regression analysis using two-way fixed-effects OLS (municipality and year fixed effects with municipality-clustered robust standard errors) as baseline, with FGLS random-effects and Mundlak correlated random-effects models as robustness checks
